message.abstract:
<jats:title>Consequences of shifting species distributions</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Climate change is causing geographical redistribution of plant and animal species globally. These distributional shifts are leading to new ecosystems and ecological communities, changes that will affect human society. Pecl
                    <jats:italic>et al.</jats:italic>
                    review these current and future impacts and assess their implications for sustainable development goals.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:italic>Science</jats:italic>
                    , this issue p.
                    <jats:related-article xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="doi" issue="6332" page="eaai9214" related-article-type="in-this-issue" vol="355" xlink:href="10.1126/science.aai9214">eaai9214</jats:related-article>
                  </jats:p>
title: Biodiversity redistribution under climate change: Impacts on ecosystems and human well-being
